events.headline: Houthi Missile Strike on Yemen Training Camp Death Toll Revised Up to 73, Deadliest of War's New Phase
events.summary: The toll from the October 19 Houthi ballistic missile strike on the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre in Shabwa, Yemen was revised upward to 73 killed, with over 200 wounded and 14 missing. Victims were mostly recruits aged 18-20 for a new 'Rapid Intervention' force; it is the deadliest single strike since Yemen's civil war resumed roughly three months ago.

events.headline: Lula Declared Winner of Brazil's Presidential Runoff Over Bolsonaro by Narrow Margin
events.summary: Official results show Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated Jair Bolsonaro's chosen candidate 51.78% to 48.22% in Brazil's presidential runoff held Oct 25. The Bolsonaro camp has not conceded, raising concerns about a contested transition.

events.headline: Trump Says US 'Could Strike Iran Tomorrow' as CENTCOM Preps Expanded Target List
events.summary: On Oct 24-25, Trump said the US 'could strike Iran tomorrow' or reach a deal, calling for a permanent end to Iran's nuclear program. CENTCOM has prepared an expanded strike-option target list for Defense Secretary Hegseth, while a DNI memo warning of 'advanced' Iranian plots against US officials abroad prompted reduced staffing at embassies in Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE.

events.headline: Tibet Earthquake Death Toll Holds at 16 as Search Operation Concludes
events.summary: The death toll from the magnitude 7.0 earthquake in Tibet's Baqen County remains at 16, with injuries revised up to 76 and no missing persons reported. More than 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds were damaged or destroyed, and over 12,000 people have been evacuated to 18 shelters.

events.headline: Vucic Concedes Defeat as Students' List Wins Decisive Majority in Serbian Election
events.summary: President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat on Oct 25 after 14 years in power as the Students' List movement won a decisive majority of roughly 135-142 of 250 seats. Turnout reached about 70%, the highest since 1992, with celebrations breaking out in Belgrade.

events.headline: Dispute Over Remains of Ambushed Salvadoran Security Technicians Deepens Haiti Gang Crisis
events.summary: Four Salvadoran Gang Suppression Force technicians were ambushed on Oct 18 in Croix-des-Bouquets, Haiti, allegedly by the Chen Mechan/400 Mawozo gang coalition. Remains recovered and presented Oct 24-25 have been disputed by El Salvador's government, which says forensic details are inconsistent with the missing personnel.

events.headline: Philippines-China Tensions Escalate With Repeated Encounters and Ambassador's 'Easily Win' Remark
events.summary: At least six to eight dangerous Philippines-China encounters have occurred since Oct 1 across Scarborough Shoal, Second Thomas Shoal, Sabina Shoal, the Spratlys and Luzon Strait, with 31 Chinese vessels recorded near four contested areas Oct 13-19 and a Chinese carrier strike group deployed to the area. Manila summoned China's ambassador after he said China 'could easily win' a conflict with the Philippines, which lawmakers called a 'thinly veiled threat.'

events.headline: Sudanese Army Drone Strikes on RSF-Held Markets Kill Over 200 Across Two Attacks
events.summary: Sudanese Armed Forces (not RSF, as initially reported) drone strikes hit two RSF-held markets: one on Oct 18-19 at a transport hub in West Kordofan killing an estimated 80-110 people, and another on Oct 19-20 at the Amiet market in the Abyei border region killing 150 or more and displacing about 8,000. South Sudan summoned Sudan's ambassador in protest and the UN condemned the strikes; local civic groups' higher estimate of around 150 for the first strike remains unconfirmed.

events.headline: Ethiopia Severs Ties With Eritrea as Border Fighting Escalates Over Tigray Rebel Support
events.summary: Ethiopia closed its Asmara embassy and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats on accusations Eritrea is arming Tigrayan rebels; Eritrea responded by severing diplomatic ties. The Tigrayan EPFAS rebel alliance struck Addis Ababa military facilities on Oct 1, and Eritrean troops near Zalambessa came under Ethiopian drone attack as fighting advanced toward Idaga Hamus, marking the worst flare-up since the 2018 peace deal.

events.headline: Venezuelan Opposition Leader María Corina Machado Returns From 10-Month Exile
events.summary: María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after roughly 10 months abroad, first appearing in Lara state before traveling to Caracas on Oct 25. She has renewed her challenge to interim President Delcy Rodríguez amid continuing political uncertainty over candidacy rules.

events.headline: Putin Agrees to Resume Trilateral Ukraine Peace Talks, Releases Detained American
events.summary: Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on October 21, during which Russia released American Stephen Hubbard, detained since 2022. A US official said Russia and Ukraine agreed to resume trilateral technical peace talks after November 10.

events.headline: Attacks on Shipping in Strait of Hormuz Surge to Wartime High
events.summary: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz hit a wartime high in October, with about 27 attacks recorded this month according to IMO figures. Oil flow through the strait has fallen to roughly 68% of its pre-war baseline, about 11.6 million barrels per day versus 17.1 million.

events.headline: UN Warns Taiz, Yemen Could Run Out of Wheat Within Weeks as Houthi Siege Tightens
events.summary: The UN warns that wheat and flour supplies in Taiz could run out within three weeks after Houthi forces tightened their blockade by seizing the city's last main road link to other areas. Food prices have risen about 50%, more than 600,000 people including 200,000+ children depend on aid, and medical supplies are nearing depletion.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Extends Martial Law in 55 Townships, Airstrikes Kill Dozens of Civilians
events.summary: Myanmar's military junta extended martial law for 90 more days across 55 townships in Sagaing, Magway, Chin, Rakhine, Karenni, Karen and Shan on Oct 18. Junta airstrikes using gyrocopters, drones and jets killed 16 people on Oct 20 across Magway, Mandalay and Chin, with separate strikes killing 7-8 civilians near the Mon-Karen border; monitors tally 65 killed by airstrikes nationwide between Oct 1-20.

events.headline: US 'Southern Spear' Strikes on Drug Boats Have Killed at Least 238 Since Campaign Began
events.summary: US military strikes on suspected drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific have killed at least 238 people across more than 79 strikes as of early October, part of the Trump administration's 'Southern Spear' campaign. A strike on Oct 4 killed 4 more. Human rights groups have called the strikes possible extrajudicial killings.

events.headline: Nigeria's Ebola Contact List Grows to 53 as Suspected Rivers State Case Tests Negative
events.summary: Nigeria's Bundibugyo-strain Ebola contact list grew from 44 to 53 people, including healthcare workers and the patient's spouse, as tracing expanded following the country's first confirmed case. A suspected case in Rivers State tested negative on Oct 23; the DRC-origin outbreak has reached five countries with over 9,500 cases and 4,200+ deaths as of Oct 18.

events.headline: France Deploys 70,000 Police, Shuts Louvre and Metro Stations Ahead of Nationwide Protests
events.summary: Ahead of Oct 24 nationwide protests, France deployed about 70,000 police and gendarmes, closed the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais, shut over 24 Metro stations, and banned demonstrations in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier while allowing restricted marches in Paris and Marseille. The measures follow rioting and looting on Oct 17 that led to roughly 2,700 detentions.

events.headline: North Korea Tells UN South Korea Fabricated DMZ Blast as Pyongyang Resumes Propaganda Broadcasts
events.summary: North Korea sent a letter to the UN Security Council on Oct 25-26 claiming South Korea fabricated a Sept 21 DMZ landmine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers. Kim Yo Jong announced the resumption of propaganda loudspeaker broadcasts along the entire border by the end of October, and a new North Korean self-propelled howitzer was spotted near the border.

events.headline: US Ambassador Pledges Up to $20 Billion in Financing for Argentina Tied to Milei's Policies
events.summary: US Ambassador Peter Lamelas said on Oct 21 that US financing agencies could mobilize up to $20 billion in investment and financing for Argentine infrastructure, energy and mining projects through the end of 2027 — nearly three times a prior $7 billion commitment. The pledge is explicitly tied to Argentina maintaining President Milei's economic policies through the 2027 election, amid an ongoing bond selloff.

events.headline: Storms Boelo and Austen Cut Power to 150,000+ Homes Across UK, France, Germany; One Dead
events.summary: Storms Boelo and Austen knocked out power to more than 150,000 homes at the weekend peak across the UK, France and Germany, with winds up to 84 mph in Scotland. At least one death was reported, and hundreds of flights were cancelled; a hospital in Freiburg was limited to emergency care only.

events.headline: Houthi Missile and Drone Barrage Targets Riyadh, Dammam, Yanbu and Najran, Intercepted
events.summary: Saudi defenses intercepted a Houthi barrage on Oct 25 including drones and a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh, a cruise missile toward Khamis Mushait, and ten ballistic missiles toward southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthis claimed seven operations targeting Riyadh airport, the Aramco facility at Yanbu, Dammam, Najran, Rabigh and Khamis Mushait, expanding the attacks beyond earlier targets near Mecca, Medina and Jeddah.

events.headline: Israeli Strike on Gaza's Islamic University Kills Three Staff as Post-Ceasefire Toll Nears 1,500
events.summary: An Israeli strike on the Islamic University of Gaza City killed three administrative staff on Oct 25, after an earlier drone strike that day wounded seven female students; about seven to eight people were killed in Gaza strikes that day overall. The Israeli military said the university strike is under review as a possible targeting error, as deaths since the ceasefire approach 1,500.

events.headline: Mali's Army Locates Major ISSP Base Near Menaka After Militants Killed 48 Civilians
events.summary: Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP) fighters killed 48 civilians near Menaka, Mali on Oct 18-19 in alleged reprisal for tip-offs to the army. The Malian army says it located a major ISSP base with fighters, equipment and logistics about 65 km southwest of Menaka on Oct 20.

events.headline: Cyclone Arnab Forecast to Make Landfall Near Andhra Pradesh on Oct 28
events.summary: The Bay of Bengal depression has intensified into Cyclone Arnab, forecast to reach severe cyclonic storm strength with sustained winds of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph before making landfall near Andhra Pradesh/Yanam on the morning of Oct 28. Authorities have identified about 570,000 vulnerable people and begun evacuations across roughly 1,400 villages and 44 towns.

events.headline: Russian Missile and Drone Barrage Hits Vinnytsia and Dnipro, Killing at Least Eight
events.summary: A Russian overnight missile and drone barrage on Oct 24-25 struck a residential building in Vinnytsia and hit Dnipro, with reported deaths ranging from 4-8 and 28-51 injured depending on the source. A separate Dnipro strike killed four and injured 22; Ukrainian officials continue tallying casualties.

events.headline: Hundreds of Thousands Join Coordinated Cost-of-Living Protests Across France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Albania
events.summary: Simultaneous demonstrations swept Europe on Oct 24: France saw 410,000-800,000 protesters and about 1,000 arrests; Italy saw protests in Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna and Florence with 371 briefly detained; Spain's Madrid saw pension protests; Portugal saw housing-crisis demonstrations; and Albania saw anti-government protests. Clashes with police involved tear gas and water cannons in several cities.

events.headline: Italy Deploys Extra Troops to Milan as Cost-of-Living Protests Turn Violent in Several Cities
events.summary: During nationwide protests on Oct 24, Italian police briefly detained 371 people and arrested 9 after stones, bottles and firecrackers were thrown in Turin, Bologna and Florence. The Meloni government deployed 500 additional soldiers to Milan and condemned the violence while protests also occurred in Rome.

events.headline: DRC's Kabila-Led FRN Coalition Pushes Toward Uvira and Kalemie as Fighting Spreads
events.summary: Joseph Kabila has formally joined the newly formed FRN (Front pour la Refondation de la Nation), merging the Congo River Alliance and M23, as its political leader. FARDC-Wazalendo forces clashed with FRN fighters around Kaziba/Kabembe from Oct 11 and in Itara-Luvungi near Kamanyola by Oct 20, with the FRN announcing its intent to march on Uvira and Kalemie.

events.headline: Albania Protesters Set Fire to Agriculture Ministry Door in Tirana Clashes, 300+ Injured
events.summary: Protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama over corruption, education and the cost of living, ongoing since mid-October, escalated on Oct 24 when demonstrators set fire to the agriculture ministry's door in Tirana. Police used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets, and more than 300 protesters and police officers were injured while government buildings, banks and shops were damaged.

events.headline: Pakistan-Afghanistan Border Clashes Continue After Moscow Talks End Without Agreement
events.summary: The 8th round of Moscow Format Consultations ended Oct 6 without a joint statement for the first time since 2017, after Pakistan and Afghanistan's Taliban failed to agree on terrorism-related language. Border clashes have continued, including a roughly four-hour exchange on Oct 17 in Kurram and fighting across the border in Paktia's Dand Patan and Zazi Aryob districts, with both sides making conflicting casualty claims.

events.headline: Venezuela Government and Opposition Agree to Review Laws Barring Opposition Candidates
events.summary: In a third round of talks at Miraflores Palace on Oct 22, Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez met opposition negotiator Dinorah Figuera and Jorge Rodríguez. The sides committed to review laws used to disqualify opposition politicians, including the Organic Comptroller Law and an anti-terrorism financing law, and discussed parity in a delegation on Bank of England-held gold. A fourth round of talks is set for Nov 11-15.

events.headline: Bangladesh Dengue Deaths Rise to 376 as Measles Toll Tops 1,200
events.summary: Bangladesh's dengue death toll reached 376 as of Oct 24-25, up from 357, with 1,898 new hospitalizations reported. The combined confirmed and suspected measles death toll reached 1,214 as of Oct 23, including 104 confirmed deaths and 1,110 suspected.

events.headline: Eurozone Inflation Jumps to 3.8%, Highest Since 2023, on Energy Costs
events.summary: Eurozone annual inflation rose to 3.8% in September 2026, up from 3.2% in August and the highest since September 2023, driven by energy inflation of 18.8% linked to Middle East conflict. The ECB meets Oct 29 with markets pricing roughly 91% odds of a further rate hike.

events.headline: Spain's Valencia Region Continues Flood Recovery After Storm Adam Killed Up to Five
events.summary: Storm Adam, a DANA weather system, brought up to 720mm of rain to Spain's Valencia and Alicante regions from Oct 17-20, killing 4-5 people and triggering confinement orders in 145 municipalities with over 1,000 emergency rescues. Prime Minister Sánchez visited affected areas and offered compensation of up to €6,000 per household as recovery continued into Oct 24-25.

events.headline: French National Assembly Rejects Revenue Section of 2027 Social Security Budget
events.summary: France's National Assembly voted 115-1 with 22 abstentions on Oct 23 to reject the revenue section of the 2027 Social Security budget, which aimed to cut the deficit from €21.8 billion to €12.7 billion. The bill now goes to the Senate on Nov 9 in its original form, as France's 10-year bond yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2002 amid ongoing protests.

events.headline: Israel Raises Military Alert to Highest Level Ahead of Oct 27 Election Citing Attack Risk
events.summary: Netanyahu warned of possible enemy attacks timed to disrupt Israel's Oct 27 election, prompting IDF Chief Zamir to raise the alert level, freeze military leave and reinforce Central Command. Opposition leader Yair Lapid requested an emergency briefing, while some officials suggested no specific threat had actually been identified.

events.headline: Ecuadorian Presidential Candidate Luisa González Ordered Into Pre-Trial Detention Over Money Laundering
events.summary: A judge in Riobamba ordered pre-trial detention on Oct 24 for Ecuadorian presidential candidate Luisa González and two co-defendants in the 'Laberinto' case, involving roughly $500,000 in alleged money laundering tied to her 2023 campaign financing. González was transferred to a prison in Riobamba, Chimborazo province.

events.headline: Cholera Outbreak Spreads Across Lake Chad Basin, Tens of Thousands of Cases in Nigeria, DRC
events.summary: A cholera outbreak driven by the Vibrio cholerae O1 Ogawa strain has spread across the Lake Chad Basin amid flooding and displacement. Nigeria has recorded over 50,000 cases and 338 deaths since January (a later WHO figure shows over 70,000 cases by Sept 20), while the DRC reported roughly 30,400 cases and about 700 deaths, later revised to nearly 49,000 cases.

events.headline: Colombian Forces Kill 10 ELN Fighters Including Commanders in Cauca Strike
events.summary: President Abelardo de la Espriella announced that Operation Onix killed 10 ELN fighters, including commanders known as 'Marcos Pacífico' and 'Ochenta,' in El Tambo, Cauca on Oct 22. Colombian officials called it the heaviest blow to the ELN in eight years.

events.headline: Cuba's Guiteras Power Plant Disconnected From Grid, Deepening Blackout Crisis
events.summary: Cuba's Guiteras thermoelectric plant was taken offline on Oct 25 due to turbine vibrations, worsening a chronic nationwide deficit of roughly 2,000 megawatts. Havana alone reported over 100 circuits interrupted amid the latest blackout wave.

events.headline: PAHO Maintains Highest Alert Level as Americas Report 1.69 Million Dengue Cases, Rising Chikungunya
events.summary: The Pan American Health Organization continues its highest Grade-3 response to multi-country dengue and chikungunya outbreaks. As of mid-September, the Americas recorded 1.69 million suspected dengue cases (3,413 severe, 571 deaths), a 58% year-on-year decrease overall but rising in Andean, Central American and Caribbean countries. Some 213,919 suspected chikungunya cases were reported across 20 countries, including renewed transmission in Guyana.

events.headline: 18-Floor Unfinished Building Collapses in Nairobi, Several Missing
events.summary: An 18-floor unfinished building with occupied ground-floor and basement shops collapsed on 9th Street in Nairobi's Eastleigh area on Oct 23. Seven people were reported missing or trapped, one woman was rescued alive, and 66 of 67 construction workers escaped. Kenya Red Cross, the military and county emergency teams are responding; the building had no occupation certificate.

events.headline: Armed Men Storm Libya's National Audit Bureau to Install Rival Deputy Head
events.summary: Masked armed men stormed the Tripoli headquarters of Libya's National Audit Bureau on Oct 21 to forcibly install Anwar al-Housh as deputy head under an appointment by the High Council of State. The Bureau suspended all operations in response. The move was condemned by UNSMIL, the United States and the United Kingdom.

events.headline: Ukraine Confirms Starshield Speeds Restored After SpaceX Lifted Two-Week Slowdown
events.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry confirmed on Oct 24 that Starshield internet speeds have been restored above 400km/h after SpaceX had capped them at 160km/h since Oct 14. Musk said the restriction stemmed from a terms-of-service violation that has now been closed. Zelensky thanked partners for resolving the issue, which had disrupted Ukrainian drone operations.

events.headline: France Confirms World's First Known Human Case of Shamonda Virus, Patient Died
events.summary: France has confirmed the world's first known human case of Shamonda virus, a midge-borne livestock virus, in a severely immunocompromised patient treated at Hospices Civils de Lyon who has since died. Health authorities identified a new 'Shamonda-Europe' strain but say there is no broader public health risk.

events.headline: Hurricane Vance Weakens to Tropical Storm, Spares Direct Hit on Puerto Vallarta
events.summary: Vance weakened from a Category 2 hurricane to a tropical storm with winds near 70 mph by Oct 25, tracking offshore south of Puerto Vallarta. Heavy rain, flash flooding and mudslides remain a threat across Colima, Nayarit, Jalisco, Michoacán, Sinaloa and Durango.

events.headline: Fire Destroys Hitler-Era 'Eagle's Nest' Retreat in Bavarian Alps, Suspect Detained
events.summary: A fire overnight on Oct 23-24 destroyed most of the Kehlsteinhaus ('Eagle's Nest'), a Hitler-era mountaintop retreat near Berchtesgaden, Germany. About 200 firefighters battled the blaze in snow and wind; no injuries were reported. A 33-year-old German suspect showing signs of mental illness was detained nearby and sent for psychiatric evaluation, with a possible political motive under investigation.

events.headline: Oil Prices Retreat From Six-Month Highs on US-Iran De-escalation Hopes
events.summary: WTI crude fell to roughly $101 a barrel and Brent to about $114-115 on Oct 26, down 1.5-2% as markets weighed hopes for US-Iran de-escalation against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure. Prices had been near six-month highs amid Gulf tensions.

events.headline: Portuguese Police Clear Housing-Crisis Protest Camps in Lisbon and Porto, Arrest 55
events.summary: Police cleared housing-crisis protest encampments in Lisbon's Rossio Square and in Porto on Oct 24-25, arresting 55 people. Protesters are demanding withdrawal of a bill that would ease evictions and end rent caps; thousands returned to the squares after the clearance.

events.headline: UK Jewish Group Declares Green Party 'Racist' Over Zionism Motion
events.summary: The Board of Deputies of British Jews voted 118-1 on Oct 25 to declare the Green Party of England and Wales 'racist' after its October conference adopted a 'Zionism is racism' motion. Board president Phil Rosenberg urged other parties not to form coalitions with the Greens, who reject the characterization.

events.headline: Magnitude 5.5-5.7 Earthquake Strikes Off Northern Sicily, Felt Widely
events.summary: An earthquake measuring magnitude 5.5-5.7 struck offshore near Capo d'Orlando in Sicily's Aeolian Islands on Oct 23 at roughly 8.8 km depth. A brief tsunami alert was issued and a magnitude 5.2 aftershock was recorded near Malfa/Salina; no major damage has been reported.

events.headline: Nigeria Evacuates 114 More Citizens From South Africa Amid Xenophobic Violence, Total Tops 2,100
events.summary: Nigeria evacuated 114 more citizens — 57 men, 23 women and 34 children — from South Africa on Oct 22 amid ongoing xenophobic and Afrophobic violence. It was the 16th such evacuation since June 10, 2026, bringing the cumulative total to 2,151 people evacuated.

events.headline: Three Hostages Held 10 Months in Central African Republic Freed, Flown to Bangui
events.summary: Three hostages — a sub-prefect and two elections authority staff — who were kidnapped in Bambouti on Dec 28, 2025, were released on Oct 19 after mediation brokered by the UN mission MINUSCA. They were flown to Bangui on Oct 22 and received by President Touadéra.

events.headline: India Issues Red Alert for Kerala Districts as Heavy Rain Raises Flood and Landslide Risk
events.summary: India's Meteorological Department issued red alerts for Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad districts on Oct 25, and for Idukki and Palakkad on Oct 26, warning of rainfall exceeding 204.4mm in 24 hours with flash flood and landslide risk. Schools were closed in the Oct 25 red-alert districts.

events.headline: China Urges US to Halt Expansion of Outbound Investment Security Restrictions
events.summary: China's Commerce Ministry said on Oct 24 it urged the United States to halt proposed expansions of outbound-investment security restrictions covering biotech, high-performance computing and hypersonic systems. Beijing called the move discriminatory and reserved the right to take countermeasures.

events.headline: Explosion and Fire at Chemical Warehouse in León, Mexico Injures Several, Hundreds Evacuated
events.summary: A large explosion and fire broke out at a chemical warehouse in the San Nicolás area of León, Guanajuato, on Oct 23-24. Several people were injured and hundreds of residents were evacuated as a precaution. No confirmed death toll has been reported.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drone Strike Hits Shopping Center in Belgorod, Russia
events.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack overnight Oct 24-25 struck the MegaGRINN shopping center in Belgorod, Russia. Russian authorities reported one person killed and 14 injured citywide; the mall itself was reportedly closed and empty at the time.

events.headline: Ukraine Reportedly Strikes Missile-Component Plant in Russia's Lipetsk Region
events.summary: Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the Energiya battery plant, which supplies missile components, in Yelets, Lipetsk Oblast on Oct 25, reportedly using Storm Shadow/SCALP missiles. The regional governor confirmed an attack on an industrial zone that injured one paramedic; the claim lacks high-reliability wire confirmation.

events.headline: Indonesia Cuts Pipeline Gas Exports to Singapore to Prioritize Domestic Supply
events.summary: Indonesia reduced pipeline gas exports to Singapore by 31 BBTUD effective Oct 24, redirecting supply from Natuna and Jambi Merang/Sumatra to domestic power needs under President Prabowo's energy security push. Singapore's Energy Market Authority says the cut represents under 2% of daily demand and may pursue contractual remedies.

events.headline: IMF Raises Egypt's Growth Forecast to 5.1% but Flags Inflation and Currency Risks
events.summary: The IMF raised its forecast for Egypt's FY2025/26 GDP growth to 5.1%, up from 4.2% in April, citing resilient economic activity, remittances and tourism. The fund flagged risks from inflation, which stood at 14.5% in August, as well as currency pressure and elevated borrowing costs.
